reference_sql:
SELECT UPPER(TRIM(p.sku)) AS clean_sku, SUM(ol.quantity) AS units
FROM products p
JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE p.sku <> UPPER(TRIM(p.sku))
GROUP BY UPPER(TRIM(p.sku))
alternatives:
WITH bad_skus AS (  -- one row per product with a sku off the standard
  SELECT product_id, UPPER(TRIM(sku)) AS clean_sku
  FROM products
  WHERE sku <> UPPER(TRIM(sku))
),
sold AS (  -- one row per product sold
  SELECT product_id, SUM(quantity) AS units
  FROM order_lines
  GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT b.clean_sku, s.units
FROM bad_skus b
JOIN sold s ON s.product_id = b.product_id

other_way.sql:
WITH bad_skus AS (  -- one row per product with a sku off the standard
  SELECT product_id, UPPER(TRIM(sku)) AS clean_sku
  FROM products
  WHERE sku <> UPPER(TRIM(sku))
),
sold AS (  -- one row per product sold
  SELECT product_id, SUM(quantity) AS units
  FROM order_lines
  GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT b.clean_sku, s.units
FROM bad_skus b
JOIN sold s ON s.product_id = b.product_id
other_way.tradeoff: Two named steps keep each grain plain, one row per product in each, but the single grouped join is shorter.

solver.query:
SELECT upper(trim(p.sku)) AS clean_sku, sum(ol.quantity) AS units
FROM order_lines ol
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = ol.product_id
WHERE p.sku <> upper(trim(sku))
GROUP BY p.product_id, upper(trim(p.sku))
